## Summary

- `src/slug.js`: `slugify` now normalizes to NFD and strips combining diacritical marks before lowercasing, so accented Latin letters (é, ü, ñ, Å, etc.) fold to their plain ASCII form instead of being dropped. A result with no letters/digits at all now falls back to `'untitled'`.
- `uniqueSlug` was rewritten: it treats the slugified base as a literal string (no more `startsWith` counting, which conflated differently-numbered bases and could reuse an already-taken suffix when there were gaps). It now checks exact membership in a `Set`, and on collision walks `n = 2, 3, ...` to find the lowest free `${base}-${n}`, which also correctly handles a title whose own slug already ends in a number (e.g. a second `"Hello World 2"` becomes `hello-world-2-2`, not colliding with `hello-world`'s numbering).
- `bin/slug.js` was unchanged — `add`/`list` output format is identical, just backed by the corrected logic.

## Summary

The bug was in `src/slug.js`: `slugify` dropped any character outside `[a-z0-9]` instead of folding accents, and `uniqueSlug` counted matching prefixes instead of finding the lowest actually-free suffix.

**Fix:**
- `slugify` now runs `title.normalize('NFD')` and strips the combining-mark range (`\u0300`-`\u036f`) before lowercasing, so é→e, ü→u, ñ→n, Å→a (and other Latin diacritics) fold instead of vanishing. If nothing alphanumeric survives, it returns `'untitled'`.
- `uniqueSlug` now checks the literal set of existing slugs and walks `base`, `base-2`, `base-3`, ... to the first one not already taken — correct even with gaps in the store or when a title's own base already ends in a number (e.g. `hello-world-2`).
- `add`/`list` in `bin/slug.js` were untouched — verified via a real CLI run that output and store format are unchanged.

**Verification:** 3 new unit tests added (5/5 pass), each fix line proven load-bearing by mutation testing (all mutations KILLED), and a real end-to-end CLI run reproduced the exact bug report (`Café Menü` → `cafe-menu`, repeat → `cafe-menu-2`) plus edge cases (`!!!` → `untitled`, next → `untitled-2`). Ledger verdict: **VERIFIED**. Report: `.oldhand/accent-slug/report.md`.

**Assumption called out in the report:** diacritic folding covers NFD-decomposable accents (the general class covering é/ü/ñ/Å); letters with no NFD decomposition (ø, ß, đ) are out of scope since the ticket didn't ask for them.

The root cause was in `search/rank.py`: candidate doc IDs were collected into a `set()` and then sorted only by `score` with `reverse=True`. Since Python's sort is stable, ties kept whatever order the set happened to iterate in — and set iteration order for strings depends on hash randomization (`PYTHONHASHSEED`), which differs between process invocations. So `--page 1` and `--page 2` (two separate CLI runs) could see different tie orderings, causing the same article to show up on both pages while another silently never appeared.

Fix: sort by `(-score, natural_key(doc_id))` where `natural_key` splits the id into text/number chunks so `doc-2` sorts before `doc-10` (not lexicographically). This makes ordering fully deterministic and satisfies the natural-order tie-break requirement.

Verified:
- Existing unit tests pass.
- Ran the same query across 5 different `PYTHONHASHSEED` values — identical output each time.
- Simulated paging across separate process invocations (varying hash seeds per page) for a query with many ties — collected results were complete, had no duplicates, and exactly matched `--all`'s output.
- Confirmed tie-break order is ascending by natural doc-id order within each score bucket.

No other files needed changes — `paging.py`'s slicing and `__main__.py`'s header/`--all` logic were already correct once `rank.ranked` became deterministic.
